title: Bucks County restaurants to try out in honor of National Hot Dog Day - NewsBreak
text:
By Michele Haddon ,
19 hours ago There are many things to enjoy as the weather warms up — one of which is hot dog season.
From backyards to ballparks, the hot dog is a simple summer favorite that’s tough to beat. And if you're willing to lean into a little creativity, you’ll discover there’s no limit to what can put on top, or even underneath, a hot dog.
So, in honor of National Hot Dog coming up on July 16, we wanted to highlight a few local eateries where you can find some of Bucks County area's most unique spins on this American classic:
The Burgerly, New Hope
Like its name implies, The Burgerly specializes in upscale, handcrafted burgers that are as eye-catching as they are flavorful. But if you’re in the mood for another handheld treat, their hot dogs are showstoppers, too. Pair either of these with an order of fries and a sauce flight to make your meal complete:
The Dam Hotdog: a split and griddle hot dog topped with pulled BBQ brisket chili, pickled cabbage and spicy mayo Dog, It's From Chicago: split and griddled hot dog topped with diced tomato, onion, house pickle, muenster, sweet onion aioli, ranchero sauce, avocado salsa and micro parsley. Go: 137 S. Main St., New Hope; 215-693-1198; theburgerly.com
Bucks County restaurant closes: Popular Jewish deli in Newtown closes its doors after three years
Lenny’s Hot Dogs, Feasterville
This unassuming little hot dog joint got its start in South Philly more than 90 years ago before opening up in Feasterville in 1998, bringing along its famous sweet pepper hash recipe and an old school Philadelphia tradition — the fish cake hot dog. To order this classic, simply ask for “The Combo,” and while you’re there, be sure to grab a container of the sweet pepper hash to take home and top on your own hot dogs. Along with The Combo, here are a few more to try:
The Combo: a classic Philly specialty featuring a hot dog and fish cake topped with sweet pepper hash Bucks County Dog: a hot dog topped with mustard, cheese and sweet pepper hash Fire Dog: a hot dog topped with hot peppers, hot chili, mustard and cheese whiz Lenny Kravitz Dog: a hot dog topped with mustard, sweet pepper hash, kraut and raw onions Details: 606 W. Street Road, Feasterville; 215-355-7616
The Speckled Egg, Lambertville
This one is located just across the river in Lambertville, New Jersey, but definitely worth checking out for its elevated take on comfort foods, served in a casual and inviting space. Their menu, which changes regularly, always features a hot dog with a twist inspired by different regional and global flavors.
Here are some of their recurring hot dog creations to keep an eye out for:
Kimchi Cheese Dog: an all beef hot dog with housemade kimchi and American cheese served on a toasted roll Muffuletta Dog: a hot dog topped with mortadella, soppressata, swiss, sharp provolone, giardiniera and olive salad Cool Ranch Hot Dog: a dry rubbed all beef hot dog with buttermilk ranch dressing crunchy cabbage on a butter toasted roll Banh Mi Hot Dog: a hot dog topped with pickled vegetables, cucumber, cilantro, jalapeños and sweet chili garlic mayo Go: 19 North Union Street, Lambertville, New Jersey; The Speckled Egg Cafe on Instagram
Bucks County bar with a rooftop view: Cocktail bar in Doylestown opened its new rooftop deck in June
Johnny Longhots, Fairless Hills
This Philly-inspired shop has a huge menu of jaw-dropping sandwiches that are so loaded up, there’s no chance you’re walking out hungry, and their hot dogs are no exception. Here are two that will fill even the biggest appetites:
Johnny’s Dirty Dog: two fried hot dogs topped with chopped fresh ribeye mixed with green peppers, onions and melted Cooper sharp cheese served in a Liscio’s seeded Italian roll Italian Hot Dog: their rendition of the Casino Dog which was a popular Trenton staple in the 70s and 80s. This beast of a sandwich comes with three all-beef hot dogs on a seeded roll topped with peppers, onions, potatoes and the option of ketchup and mustard. Go: 545 S. Oxford Valley Road, Fairless Hills; 267-202-6009; johnnylonghotsbucks.com
Snackdown Grille, Quakertown
Get ready to put your hunger in a headlock at this wrestling-themed eatery inside the Quakertown Farmer’s Market, where you’ll find more than 20 different loaded hot dogs, many of which carry names inspired by popular wrestlers or their signature moves. Some of their Main Event dogs include:
Pedigree Dog: a hot dog with baked beans, homemade BBQ sauce, cheese, bacon and mustard Samoan Dog: a hot dog with pepperoni, homemade BBQ sauce, bacon, cheese and ranch Elite Chili Dog: a hot dog with chili, bacon, mustard, cheese and onion Go: Quakertown Farmers Market, 201 Station Road, Quakertown; Snackdown Grille on Instagram
Great burgers in Bucks County: These Bucks County spots are known for their top-notch burgers
Reporter Michele Haddon covers local news, small business, food and drink, economic revitalization, art and culture for The Intelligencer and Bucks County Courier Times at PhillyBurbs.com. Please consider supporting local journalism with a subscription.
